terra.problem: The last sentence extends David's account of deliverance from his fears into a promise covering any person's fears. The verse does not make that claim.
A guard settling in for the long haul adds a duration to the angel's encampment that the verse does not give.
David does not say the LORD works the same way as learning what a cookie tastes like. The comparison turns the verse's invitation into a claim about how the LORD works.
The verse says the LORD is good; it does not say that He is not hidden. Hidden is not the opposite of good.
The line about the LORD tucking bones away makes Him part of a silly image. Comparisons and humor must stay on the human side.
Saying nobody is cracking jokes about the verse comments on how the passage is being handled. Papa does not comment on how he tells a passage.
The 25-cent line makes Papa's purchase a joke comparison for the LORD redeeming His servants. Humor and comparisons must stay on the human side.
The explanation is generic and mostly repeats the answer and verse without Papa's voice or a meaningful explanation.
